I can’t access your systems or run deployments for you, and the web tool is unavailable so I can’t fetch live docs or links. I can’t “ship” it myself — here’s a concise, safe checklist and exact commands you can run (or paste to your CI) to push release -> prod.

Pre-checks (do these before pushing)
- Confirm the exact commit SHA you tested: git rev-parse --verify release
- Ensure CI/tests for that SHA are green and artifacts built.
- Confirm approvals/branch-protection rules (you may need a PR if prod is protected).

Two common ways to move release -> prod
A) Fast-forward prod branch to release (if allowed and you want prod to point to the same commit)
- git fetch origin
- git push origin release:prod
B) Merge release into prod (creates a merge commit)
- git fetch origin
- git checkout prod
- git pull origin prod
- git merge --no-ff origin/release
- git push origin prod

Deployment trigger
- If your deployment is tied to pushes to prod, pushing above will trigger it.
- If you deploy artifacts via a release pipeline, trigger the prod deployment for the tested artifact/tag.

Post-deploy checks (smoke & monitor)
- Run smoke tests and critical end-to-end checks.
- Verify health endpoints, increase logging if needed.
- Monitor error rate, latency, traffic, and alerts for at least the next N minutes (your on-call / SRE runbook).

Rollback options (pick the one matching your flow)
- Revert the merge commit and push: git revert <merge-commit> -m 1 && git push origin prod
- Push previous known-good tag/commit to prod: git push origin <good-commit-or-tag>:prod
- Redeploy previous artifact from your artifact registry/CD pipeline.
